- **Premise note**: the pin lives in PR #7089's test suite (in flight at filing time), so it was not re-verified against `origin/main`; the hold does not depend on it having merged.

**Read-only factual correction on the hold's cost premise. ⛔ Not a claim, no label changed, no re-grade — the disposition is triage's and the maintainer's.** All facts verified on `origin/main` @ `c41828d` before writing.

The recorded restart condition includes *"the next Turso driver batch (re-weigh the probe cost there)"*. A Turso batch just landed (#8198, merged `a5dcb74`), it touched this exact class, and the re-weigh comes out differently than the hold assumed.

### ① The round trip the refusal "exists to avoid" is already being paid, unconditionally

The pinned residue case states the premise as settled fact (`turso-remote-autonumber-refusal.test.ts:311`):

> `RemoteTransport.upsert` emits `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, and whether that statement merges or inserts is knowable only after it runs — **a round trip this refusal exists to avoid**.

But `RemoteTransport.upsert` (`remote-transport.ts:1210`) already performs that round trip on **every** call:

```ts
await this.client!.execute({ sql, args: values });        // the INSERT … ON CONFLICT
const result = await this.client!.execute({               // ← already paid, every time
  sql: `SELECT * FROM "${object}" WHERE "id" = ?`,
  args: [toUpsert.id],
});
const rows = this.mapRows(result);
return rows[0] || toUpsert;
```

The pin's own assertion reads that round trip's result — `expect(inserted.case_number).toBeNull()` is reading the row this `SELECT` returned. **The NULL is already in hand at zero additional cost.**

And the detection is simpler than the premise frames it: this leg does not require distinguishing *merged* from *inserted*. It requires noticing that an autonumber column came back NULL, which is one field read on a row the method already has.

### ② A diagnostic sink now exists in this class, and did not when the hold was written

#8198 gave `RemoteTransport` a one-way sink — `private diagnosticSink` (`remote-transport.ts:853`), registered via `setDiagnosticSink()`, wired by `TursoDriver` at construction as `setDiagnosticSink((message) => this.logger.warn(message))` (`turso-driver.ts:373`). So the *"silently"* half of this card's title is now separable from the refuse-or-generate half: warning an operator costs a log line, not a round trip.

### What this does NOT establish

- ⛔ It does not say the leg should be **refused**. Refusing after the write already happened is a different act from refusing before it, and that trade-off is untouched by the above.
- `RemoteTransport` has **no autonumber or schema awareness** — grep for `autonumber`/`autoNumber` in that file returns nothing, so it cannot today tell which column is an autonumber. Closing this leg needs the driver to hand that rule down. That is plumbing with two established precedents in the same class (`setFilterColumnSql`, `setDiagnosticSink`), not a round trip — but it is real work, and I have not measured it.
- The deferred-half (A) relationship to remote autonumber generation is unchanged.

**Net**: the disposition may well stay held — but if it does, it should rest on a premise that is true. The stated one is not.

Findings-triage round (2026-08-13): **promoted** `finding` → `pm:queue`, type Bug. The previous hold's cost premise was measured false on `origin/main` @ `c41828d` (comment above, 2026-08-13): the post-write `SELECT` round trip is already paid unconditionally by `RemoteTransport.upsert`, so "detecting this leg costs the round trip the refusal exists to avoid" no longer holds — the NULL is already in hand, and #8198's `diagnosticSink` gives the class a loud channel that did not exist when the hold was written.

**Promoted scope (deliberately narrow):** make the silent leg loud, nothing more. The driver hands the autonumber-column rule down to `RemoteTransport` (same plumbing precedent as `setFilterColumnSql` / `setDiagnosticSink`), and when an upsert on this leg comes back with a NULL autonumber column, emit a warning through the existing sink naming the object, column and id. Update the `[known residue, not fixed]` pin to assert the warning fires. ⛔ Out of scope, unchanged by this promotion: refusing the leg post-write (a different act than the pre-write gate, untouched trade-off) and generating autonumbers on remote (stays behind the #6944 disposition-A appetite door). Not a contract accept/reject change — observability restoration on a declared-but-unfulfilled column.

Size/model suggestion: S–M, sonnet/opus; consumer test is the existing `turso-remote-autonumber-refusal.test.ts` residue pin.

## ACCEPT the implementation — holding the ready-flip until CI converges

Reviewed against the branch and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report's self-description. PR #8412 @ `6f1dc1f`, 3 files, +296/−19, path surface clean.

### ⚠️ My mechanism assumption was wrong, and so was the promoted shape — an existing pin says so

I dispatched this with *"the driver hands the autonumber-column rule down to `RemoteTransport`, same plumbing precedent as `setFilterColumnSql` / `setDiagnosticSink`"*, echoing triage's promoted scope. I flagged it as an assumption to refute. **It is refuted, by a guard neither of us cited** — `turso-remote-autonumber-refusal.test.ts`, in a block titled `[#6944] the layer the refusal is raised on, pinned`:

```ts
expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(RemoteTransport.prototype).some((m) => /autonumber|sequence/i.test(m)))
  .toBe(false);
```

with a sibling case *"TursoDriver DOES see it, in remote mode, which is why it can"*. Teaching the transport that rule would have gone red there, **correctly** — #6944 already decided this layering and pinned the decision. The driver-side placement is the one the existing tests actively endorse, and it needs no plumbing at all: `TursoDriver.upsert` already holds both the returned row and `autoNumberFields[object]` at the same frame, and its `logger.warn` *is* the sink `setDiagnosticSink` forwards to. Net new mechanisms: zero. Confirmed the other half of my assumption too — `RemoteTransport` still has no autonumber/schema awareness.

### Verified

- **The pin asserts both halves and says why.** The NULL is unchanged (accept/reject untouched) *and* the silence is gone, with an in-test note that if the NULL half ever flips, the change was a refusal or a generator and owes the #6944 appetite-door conversation. That is the guard that stops this from quietly becoming the refusal it was scoped not to be.
- **False positives were designed against, not hoped away.** The check reads the **result** row, not the request — a merging upsert leaves the slot empty in the request too, so a request-shaped rule would have warned on the one leg #6944 measured as correct. Three silence controls pin it: the MERGE leg, an object with no `auto_number` field, and a caller-supplied number on this same leg (the seed-replay / import path).
- **Reverse verification runs both directions**, predicted first. ① fix reverted → exactly 1 red, on the *warning* half, with the NULL assertion staying green (proving the pin reports "the silence came back", not "upsert broke"). ② predicate dropped so it over-fires → exactly 2 red, the MERGE-leg and caller-supplied controls, **with the pin itself green**. ② is the half ① cannot prove: the pin alone cannot tell a correct warning from a wolf-crying one.
- **Changeset `patch` is right** — no export moves, the new member is `private`, no caller-visible behaviour change; only an operator log line where there was silence. (I checked whether my #8198 `minor` argument transfers; it does not, same as on #8269.)

### The open question — decided: ship **A**, as it was

Whether to distinguish *"this upsert inserted a NULL"* from *"this upsert merged onto a row that was already null"*. A (shipped) reports observed state and never claims which leg ran; B pre-reads to tell them apart. **A is correct**: the actionable fact is identical either way — a persisted row whose declared `auto_number` column is empty, named by id — and B would buy back exactly the per-write round trip whose absence is the reason this card was promotable at all. ⛔ Not a follow-up card; if a caller ever needs the distinction, that is #6944's appetite door, not a probe.

### #8413 — verified filed, and it narrows this card's own title

Open, unassigned, unlabelled, for triage. It measures that the Turso **remote** face drops `unique` entirely (zero `unique`/`UNIQUE` occurrences across `remote-transport.ts`; declared-unique column takes duplicates on remote while local rejects the identical write), so `upsert` with `conflictKeys` raises a raw `SqliteError` / `SQLITE_ERROR` with no `status` — not an ADR-0112 envelope.

⚠️ Consequence for **this** card, stated by the dev and worth carrying: #7099 is titled for the *"id **or** `conflictKeys`"* leg, but on remote only the **`id` half is reachable today** — the `conflictKeys` half throws before it can merge or insert. PR #8412 covers the leg as specified; its effective coverage is the `id` half, through no fault of the implementation.

**Next:** CI still converging (23 checks, several `in_progress`). ⛔ No flip on an `in_progress` read. All gate jobs `completed: success` → ready → merge queue → follow to MERGED. `check:objectui-pin-fresh` and `check-dev-prereqs` reds reported from the dev's worktree are expected to be absent in CI, as on #8269.
